lead: A floating button: a circular or square button fixed to a corner of the viewport, for page-wide actions (back to top, support, create). Its position uses the theme style's margins; stack several vertically with `FloatButton.Group`, and use `FloatButton.BackTop` for back to top. The examples below are each contained in their own box; in real use they are fixed to a corner of the whole window.

group.title: Group
group.description: In a circular group each button keeps its own shadow and a gap; a square group is joined end to end.

back-top.title: Back to top
back-top.description: Appears once scrolled past `visibilityHeight`; a click scrolls smoothly back to the top, or jumps when the system asks for reduced motion. `target` sets the scroll container.
back-top.line: Line {n} — scroll down, the button appears after 120px.

corner.title: Corner and label
corner.description: `corner` picks one of the four corners; a square button can carry a label.

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.description: Theme styles define in `float-button.css` the size, the distance from the corner (`--_ix` / `--_iy`) and the gap inside a group; the shadow is the theme style's overlay shadow. The antd theme style follows measurements of the antd site: 40px, an 18px icon, 24px from the right and 48px from the bottom, a 16px gap in a circular group.
styling.button: `data-shape` / `data-variant` / `data-corner`; `data-in-group` inside a group (then it is no longer fixed itself); `data-has-label` when it has a label
styling.group: `data-shape` / `data-corner`; fixed to the corner, with the buttons stacked vertically
